result.title: Recall or Relearn? A Mixture of In-Context Experts for Recurring Concept Drift
result.summary: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) are being applied to Web data streams such as network intrusion detection, where they adapt by updating the labelled rows of their context without retraining. When a past concept returns after leaving the context, a TFM faces a recall-or-relearn decision between restoring stored rows of the concept and relearning it from new labels. We propose MICE (Mixture of In-Context Experts), a training-free learner that cuts the stream into segments at detected changes. It merges a closed segment into a stored context when the TFM's estimated additional error on the segment is within a tolerance, under a capacity limit on stored contexts. A fast level weights the stored contexts and first-in-first-out (FIFO) windows by the log-loss of their predictions on the last labelled batch. We show that, with pure stored contexts and a margin condition, this fast level gains over relearning, in expected accuracy, the normalised positive area between the stored context's accuracy and the TFM's learning curve, up to a first-batch term. A slow level mixes the fast level's prediction with that of the FIFO window of the last labelled rows and bounds the discounted half-Brier regret of MICE against this window at every time. Learning curves measured beforehand predict the ordering of the observed recall gains. MICE outperforms reset, which empties the context at detected drifts, on grid streams with random boundary phases. Merging keeps fewer experts than pools that store every segment, and with fixed segmentation a time-matched snapshot pool matches MICE on the shifted grid. On real streams, MICE has the highest mean accuracy of all policies we compare.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MICE：面向表格基础模型的免训练流式学习器，按检测到的漂移切分数据流，以容量受限的存储上下文与 FIFO 窗口构成快慢两层「上下文专家」混合，按近期标注批次上的 log-loss 加权，并给出相对重学习的收益分析与 regret 界。
AI.relevance_reason: 「召回还是重学」的取舍与按近期证据为多份缓存状态加权，可能启发 LVR 中复用缓存 latent 状态还是重算的决策，以及多潜在假设的证据筛选与容量/成本权衡，可供核查其加权与容量规则的可迁移性。
